Riverside Public Library — Summer Reading Program


Our free Summer Reading Program runs from July 1 to August 15. It is open to all readers aged 6 to 16. To join, simply bring your library card to the front desk and pick up a reading log.


Read any five books and return your log by August 20 to receive a free book bag. Readers who finish ten books will also get a ticket to the Science Museum. Audiobooks count, but comic books do not.


Every Saturday at 10 a.m., volunteers from Riverside College lead story sessions in Room 2. Parents are welcome, but children under 8 must be with an adult. If you do not have a library card, you can apply online or at the desk. Please bring a document showing your home address.


For more information, call 0771-555-2046 or visit the desk between 9 a.m. and 6 p.m., Monday to Saturday.

p2.title: Task · Passage
p2.text:
Many people believe that working from home makes employees lazy. A recent study suggests the opposite. Researchers followed 1,600 workers at a travel company for two years. Half of them worked from home, while the others stayed in the office.


The home workers turned out to be about 13 percent more productive. They took fewer breaks, had fewer sick days and did not waste time on the road. They also reported feeling happier. As a result, far fewer of them quit their jobs during the study.


However, working from home is not perfect. About half of the home workers later asked to return to the office, at least for some days of the week. They said they felt lonely and missed talking with their colleagues. Some also worried that their managers would forget them when it was time for promotion.


The researchers believe the best choice may be a mix: two or three days at home and the rest in the office. In this way, companies can save money on office space while workers still enjoy the social side of work.
